release.body:
The last release shipped mute, search, and archive. This one finishes blocking. A blocked user is now hidden from invites, chat previews, message timelines, search results, and notifications, and their messages stop counting toward unread badges. Video attachments work end to end across devices. The offline notice now covers every screen. The White Noise app database is encrypted at rest. Three security issues in the Marmot Development Kit were fixed.

Between 2026-04-16 and now, the mobile app merged 30 pull requests, the Rust backend merged 36, and the Marmot Development Kit shipped version 0.8.0. No migration required for users; the app handles encryption migration on first launch.

issue.title: fix: create android release checksums
issue.body: ## Summary - add `.sha256` sidecar generation for Fastlane-staged Android APK and AAB artifacts - cover the Android Fastlane staging path in release automation tests - document that Fastlane creates Android checksum sidecars ## Why The Fastlane release flow staged Android artifacts without the `.sha256` files expected by the release process. The checksum now hashes the final staged artifact bytes and writes the standard ` ` format so `shasum -a 256 -c` works from the artifact directory. ## Verification - `just test-release-scripts` - `just release-build-android-staging` - `just release-build-android-production` - `shasum -a 256 -c *.sha256` in both staged Android release directories ---

`29-36`: _⚡ Quick win_ **The technical claim about Flutter's `InputDecorator` behavior is incorrect, and the proposed fix would introduce a bug.** Flutter's `InputDecorator` calculates `minContainerHeight` as: ``` minContainerHeight = (isDense || isCollapsed || expands) ? inputHeight : kMinInteractiveDimension ``` This formula does **not** check whether `contentPadding` is `null` or non-null. Since `WnSearchField` does not set `isDense`, `isCollapsed`, or `expands`, the `minContainerHeight` will always be `kMinInteractiveDimension` (48.0 dp), regardless of whether `contentPadding` is explicitly set. Setting `contentPadding` only affects the `contentHeight` calculation (padding is added); it does not bypass the 48 px minimum. Therefore, the rendered `TextField` will enforce the 48 px floor as Flutter's `InputDecorator` always does, making the `kMinInteractiveDimension` clamp in `heightOf()` **necessary and correct**. Removing the clamp as proposed would cause `heightOf()` to return values below 48 px on small screens, while the actual rendered `TextField` remains at 48 px due to Flutter's enforcement, creating the exact mismatch the review attempts to fix. > Likely an incorrect or invalid review comment.

`29-36`: _⚡ Quick win_ **The technical claim about Flutter's `InputDecorator` behavior is incorrect, and the proposed fix would introduce a bug.** Flutter's `InputDecorator` calculates `minContainerHeight` as: ``` minContainerHeight = (isDense || isCollapsed || expands) ? inputHeight : kMinInteractiveDimension ``` This formula does **not** check whether `contentPadding` is `null` or non-null. Since `WnSearchField` does not set `isDense`, `isCollapsed`, or `expands`, the `minContainerHeight` will always be `kMinInteractiveDimension` (48.0 dp), regardless of whether `contentPadding` is explicitly set. Setting `contentPadding` only affects the `contentHeight` calculation (padding is added); it does not bypass the 48 px minimum. Therefore, the rendered `TextField` will enforce the 48 px floor as Flutter's `InputDecorator` always does, making the `kMinInteractiveDimension` clamp in `heightOf()` **necessary and correct**. Removing the clamp as proposed would cause `heightOf()` to return values below 48 px on small screens, while the actual rendered `TextField` remains at 48 px due to Flutter's enforcement, creating the exact mismatch the review attempts to fix. > Likely an incorrect or invalid review comment.

_🧹 Nitpick_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**`32.h` in `chatsHeaderH` is a magic number that should track `_filterChipsHeight`.**

`8.h + 32.h` is the total chip-row area in chats view, where `8.h` is the gap and `32.h` is the chips widget height. This equals `_filterChipsHeight.h` (the same value used for the archive pinned header, which bundles the 8.h top-padding inside `Padding`). If `_filterChipsHeight` is ever updated, the chips height in `chatsHeaderH` would silently drift.

<details>
<summary>♻️ Proposed simplification</summary>

```diff
- final chatsHeaderH = archiveHeaderH + 8.h + 32.h;
+ final chatsHeaderH = archiveHeaderH + _filterChipsHeight.h;
```
</details>

issue.title: Remove chat list subscription from chat screen and use chat summary
issue.body: ## Description This PR uses the new method to get a single chat summary by group id and account id to remove the chat list stream subscription from the chat screen. By doing so, the use chat profile hook can be replaced by the use chat summary not only in the chat screen bun in the chat invite and chat info screens **Commit by commit:** - Moves chat summary type from chat list file in bridge to chat summary file. This because the new method to get chat summary will be used from screens that are not the chat list, so placing it in the chat list is confusing. - Adds to the bridge the new method to get a chat a single chat summary - Adds the hook to fetch chat summary from rust crate - Adds util to process how to display a chat summary (that will be used in multiple screens after) - Changes chat screen to stop subcribing to chat list and use chat summary, replacing use chat profile - Replaces use chat profile in chat info screen by chat summary - Same for chat invite screen ⚠️ With this change when a user is removed from a group it updates on navigation, If the removed user is in that chat screen when removed, it won't immediately see the warning. This is because the chat stream has no event to notify this, only the chat list had. @jgmontoya is already working on this [#806](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/issues/806), but won't fit for thursday's release. IMO the temporary downgrade in removal UX is not that terrible compared with the performance con of susbcribing to all chat list events on every chat when it is not really needed. But if you disaggree, then this should be merged after we have the stream on rust side and use it here. ## Type of Change - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) - [X] 🧹 Code refactor - [ ] ✅ Build configuration change - [ ] 📝 Documentation - [ ] 🗑️ Chore - [ ] 🧪 Tests ## How I Tested This - From another device, removed me from a group. Checked that once entering that chat I saw the removed warning - Blocked users logic works the same as the other PR: once I block a user, I don't see any message from that user until unblocked ## Checklist - [x] `just precommit` passes - [ ] Related issue linked (`Closes #NNN`) - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated (if user-visible change) - [ ] Screenshots added (for UI changes) ---

@erskingardner
- It makes sense that at MLS level we need to keep processing things form blocked users, I'm not against that
- What I think is that visibility of messages could be stored in rust to avoid this filtering in flutter side logic. (I think it should be more efficient cause the visibility of a message for an account could be stored in db and no need to recalculate visibility every time we enter a chat). 
- If nostr mute lists are not enough for block feature (because to emulate block behavior form other apps we need to know when it was blocked), then a MIP makes sense to me.

🙏 If we do ship this PR in this release, I would still like to have some things changed before merge:

What I don't like about this PR is that it is using the chat list in the chat screen and refreshing it when I wanted it to be removed from that screen before this.
2. Renaming this feature to "Mute". I think it would be more accurate wording and avoid confusions with how block works in other apps. 

🙏🙏  **One petition more**
 If we release this, I would still like to work after this is merged with @jgmontoya to move as much as possible the filtering logic from flutter to rust side, hopefully for the next release before Oslo.  I think this hooks for chat list and chat messages are getting too complex... Could we agree on that in exchange for merging this for this release?

comment.body:
@pepina-dev I hear you. There are some real constraints in our world that those centralized services don't have to deal with though...

The biggest of which is that we need to process enough MLS to decrypt/authenticate and distinguish application messages from commits/proposals. Commits/proposals from blocked members still need to be processed to keep the group state coherent unless the product decision is “blocking also removes/forks group membership,” which is a much larger protocol decision.

We _maybe_ could delete them after processing but that feels brittle to me. 

If we really want blocking that will work the way that you describe it's almost certainly going to need to be a Marmot protocol level concern. 

One thing that we might do (not perfect, I'll admit up front) would be to ship this now, and test it with some real users in Oslo later this month and get real user feedback. If it's clear that your way is much better, then we should take it seriously and do the work to make it protocol level so all clients will handle it the same. What do you think?

No no no. I realized that emir had already introduced a fetch of the whole chat list in the chat screen just to check if I was removed from the chat or not. I asked @jgmontoya to make a method to avoid that and get just the required info instead of the whole chat list.

review.body:
I really dislike this approach of filtering everywhere in the flutter when the rust side already knows that the user is blocked.  It feels it makes  everything more complicated for flutter in lots of screens and if our goal is to keep this UI layer as simple as possible, for me this logic that is more complicated, belongs to the rust side. 

Some things here feel like an overkill. For example, we don't need to fetch all the blocked pubkeys through the chat list stream in a DM chat screen  to then decide if that single user is blocked. It should be easier, no chat list stream needed at all.

**From product perspective**

I don't like this behaviour either: 
- I should be able to see the past messages with a blocked user, and only not seeing the new messages since I blocked.  But here, since I block, all the past messages are hidden too
- If I unblock, I shouldn't see the messages that the user sent me while was blocked. But here, if I unblock a user, I can see all the messages that he sent me while I had blocked him. This for me is an important part of the blocking feature, simply "loosing" the connection with that person while block with no way to know if that person wrote to me or not. For exes, stalkers, etc this behaviour helps to reduce anxiety a lot, you simply can't know what they wrote while blocked even if at a moment of weakness you unblock them back. 

I tried for example blocking Javier in whatsapp and signal and it both and it behaves that way. After blocking him, I can enter the chat and see the previous messages before I blocked him, but I can't receive new messages. He sent messages to me while blocked and even after unblocking him, I can't see the messages he sent in the meantime.


**Strong opinion**
I'd rather release without blocking users logic (by simply removing the buttons or hiding them with a feature flag) and build it right, moving this filtering behavior to rust side and making it behave as blocking users works in whatsapp (which I think is the one that has the best UX for blocking)

issue.body: ## Summary - Hide invites, chat previews, message timelines, and search results from blocked users - Suppress blocked senders from new chat updates and notifications - Refresh block state from the Rust mute list so the UI stays in sync after block and unblock actions - Exclude `widgetbook/**` from the root analyzer so Widgetbook is checked in its own package context ## Testing - Added and updated unit and widget tests for chat list, chat screen, invite flow, message search, chat list search, and notification handling - Ran `just generate` - Ran `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` for the root app and for `widgetbook` - Ran `just precommit` successfully --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * App-wide blocking: block/unblock now hides blocked users across chats, messages, searches, invites, and notifications; blocked invites are auto-redirected/hidden and unread/preview counts are sanitized. * **Chores** * Analyzer configuration updated and minor dependency revision applied. * **Tests** * Extensive tests added/updated covering blocking, filtering, invites, notifications, chat summary, message/search filtering, and related UI flows.
